title: SM-1 — Studio Full-Text Search Delivery
summary: clean Studio search inputs and rank title, headings, body text, and code terms in one document-level static index
content_html:
SM-1 — Studio Full-Text Search Delivery

Status

SM-1.2 automated acceptance is complete. Studio extraction, generated-query behavior, ranking, scope isolation, and the measured payload are accepted below. Compact-result presentation remains with the user for direct review and feedback before SM-1.3 begins.

Complete Result

Studio Docs Viewer search returns one deterministic document result for title, section-heading, body-text, and authored code queries. Ranking strongly prefers title over headings and headings over body or code matches. Parent title, document identity, and update dates remain available as structural or display metadata but are not searchable Studio terms.

Boundary

SM-1 adds Studio headings, readable body prose, inline code, and fenced code to the common v2 inverted index. It retains parent title only as non-searchable display context, rebuilds the complete Studio search index after a search-relevant document change, and keeps result presentation compact.

It does not change the v2 schema or shared browser query path established by DSI-1, enable body text for another scope, change Catalogue Search, add snippets or highlighting, create section results or deep links, add stemming/synonyms/typo correction, index link destinations or report configuration, or introduce another tokenizer or search engine.

Studio Full-Text Search Index owns the proposed data shape, extraction boundary, ranking, representative examples, and prototype payload findings. Docs Viewer Search Tokenizer owns shared term semantics.

Delivery Steps

The verification tables are initial ceilings, not quotas. Confirm or reduce the relevant table after inspecting that step's exact owners; expand it only when implementation reveals a new credible risk and the step is updated before proceeding.

SM-1.0 — Readiness And Sequence

  • [x] Confirm DSI-1 is complete and record its accepted Studio metadata-only v2 index as the implementation and payload baseline.
  • [x] Confirm Studio heading/body/code inclusion fits the shared field-policy seam without a schema, tokenizer, runtime, or scope-name branch.
  • [x] Confirm the broad shared Markdown rendering/parsing owner can expose visible headings, prose, inline code, and fenced code while excluding non-visible configuration.
  • [x] Confirm SM-1.1 owns extraction and Studio policy, SM-1.2 owns representative acceptance and payload measurement, and neither step changes another scope.
  • [x] Record genuine extraction, scope-isolation, or payload stop conditions, then stop for implementation approval.

No executable verification is budgeted for this read-only step. The production extractor, generated Studio delta, exact file set, test changes, and final payload measurement belong to SM-1.1 or SM-1.2.

Gate: Review readiness against the completed DSI-1 baseline before any SM-1 production or test implementation begins.

Record: Completed 2026-08-13. DSI-1 is complete and closed. The accepted Studio baseline is the single docs_viewer_search_index_v2 producer in build_search.py, the flat search_fields policy in docs_scopes.json and docs_scope_config.py, the sole postings query and scorer in docs-viewer-search.js, and the existing whole-index search rebuild owned by the write service and watcher. Studio currently indexes title, parent_title, exact identity, and exact last_updated; its current generated baseline is 236 documents, 630 terms, and 140,666 raw bytes. The document table already retains identity, URL, update, parent, and display metadata independently of which fields emit postings.

The existing field-policy allowlist already contains heading, body, and code, build_search_index_v2 accepts those fields generically, and the browser query owner already intersects and scores their postings. SM-1 therefore needs only a Studio policy change: enable title, heading, body, and code, while removing parent_title, identity, and last_updated from Studio postings. Parent title remains in the document table for compact result context. Other scopes retain their explicit metadata-only field lists. No schema, tokenizer, loader, query-path, scope-name branch, or full-text mode is required.

studio/shared/python/markdown_renderer.py is the broad Markdown authority. Its common Markdown-it parser exposes heading, inline, inline-code, fence, code-block, raw-HTML, script, and style boundaries, and its HTML text projection already ignores attributes and script/style contents. The exact report-source owner in docs_report_source.py can project a validated structural report declaration away before extraction. Together these existing seams can expose non-duplicate authored headings, readable prose, inline code, and fenced code without indexing front matter, link destinations, media attributes, raw markup, report configuration, or script/style contents. SM-1.1 should add one small field-aware extraction result to that shared renderer and consume it from the current search builder; it must not read generated by-ID payloads as a second source model or duplicate report parsing.

Readiness correction 2026-08-13: parent_title is not a useful Studio full-text retrieval field because it can make every child match a broad hierarchy label without matching its own authored content. It remains display metadata only. The existing scorer's relative parent_title and body/code weights are therefore inactive for Studio and need no production change. SM-1.2 remains acceptance-only: it owns generated query evidence, deterministic rank confirmation, corpus measurements, non-Studio path comparison, and the temporary manual presentation check.

The expected SM-1.1 review shape is the existing Studio scope record, shared Markdown renderer, search builder, and their current focused Python/shared-query fixtures: roughly 100–180 production/config lines and 80–140 focused test/fixture lines, plus the regenerated Studio index and delivery evidence. Stop before absorbing the change if exact visible-source extraction would require duplicating Markdown/report/media resolution, if the shared renderer cannot separate eligible text without indexing non-visible configuration, if a schema/tokenizer/reader/cache or scope-name branch becomes necessary, if another scope or Catalogue path changes, or if the production/test shape materially exceeds this estimate. Gate outcome: ready for SM-1.1 implementation review and explicit approval; no production code, tests, prototype, implementation search build, or executable verification changed or ran during readiness. The routine docs watcher regenerated only this delivery record's existing by-ID, Recent, and metadata-only search projections.

SM-1.1 — Studio Source Extraction And Field Inclusion

  • [x] Enable heading, body, and code fields only in Studio's shared v2 search policy.
  • [x] Extract the authored title, non-duplicate Markdown headings, readable body prose, inline code, and fenced code through the shared Markdown rendering/parsing contract.
  • [x] Exclude front matter other than approved display/context fields, generated markup, report-block declarations, link destinations, media paths, scripts, styles, timestamps, and punctuation-only fragments.
  • [x] Apply the shared tokenizer without adding Studio-only normalization or query behavior.
  • [x] Retain doc_id, viewer URL, last_updated, parent_id, and parent_title only for identity, navigation, display, rebuild ownership, or deterministic tie-breaking.
  • [x] Make an affected Studio search build recompute the complete Studio v2 index while leaving safe document-payload builds targeted.

Gate: Studio extraction and field inclusion work through the shared v2 owners, focused evidence passes, and non-Studio outputs are unchanged. Stop before acceptance and payload review.

Record: Completed 2026-08-13. Studio's existing search_fields record now enables only title, heading, body, and code; parent title, exact identity, and update metadata remain in each document-table row without emitting postings. No other scope policy changed. The shared Markdown renderer now exposes one field-aware result after the existing Markdown-it render: duplicate title headings are omitted, other visible headings are deduplicated, inline and fenced code are separated from prose, HTML attributes are ignored, image alt text remains readable, and script/style contents are skipped.

build_search.py activates extraction from the configured content fields rather than a scope-name branch. It parses the exact report contract once for a content-enabled scope, projects structural report declarations away, replaces authored semantic tokens with their visible labels through the existing semantic-token parser, removes configured media tokens, and feeds the remaining canonical Markdown through the shared renderer. Metadata-only scopes bypass report parsing and body extraction. The v2 schema, tokenizer, browser loader/query path, scorer, whole-index orchestration, targeted document-payload behavior, and Catalogue Search owners did not change.

The implementation stayed within the readiness shape at 174 net production/config lines and 92 net focused test/fixture lines. One representative builder fixture covers duplicate-title headings, Markdown and raw-HTML headings/prose/code, image alt text, semantic-token labels, and negative front-matter, URL, report, media, script/style, date, identity, and field-leak cases. The shared tokenizer fixture gained only the missing DOCS_VIEWER_BASE_URL example. The first focused Python run reported 1 failed and 56 passed because the negative word child also appeared visibly in another fixture title; replacing that assertion with an opaque immutable structural ID corrected the fixture without changing production code. The rerun reported 57 passed.

Further focused evidence passed: the direct JavaScript tokenizer/query contract; 15 existing shared Markdown renderer tests; explicit Python lint over the builder, renderer, and focused test; Python compilation; and git diff --check. The watcher generated the complete Studio index, and an explicit $HOME/miniconda3/bin/python3 docs-viewer/build/build_search.py --scope studio --write repeat wrote zero and skipped the identical index. The generated Studio index contains 236 document rows, declares exactly title, heading, body, and code, and every posting uses only those fields. Before/after SHA-256 comparisons were identical for Analysis, Processing, Notes, and dotlineform search indexes; the bounded path diff contains no Catalogue file. Updating this delivery evidence also regenerated its routine Studio by-ID, Recent, Backlinks, and search projections. Gate outcome: SM-1.1 is complete and parked for review; stop before SM-1.2 representative queries, payload measurements, and manual presentation acceptance.

SM-1.2 — Query Acceptance And Payload Review

  • [x] Rebuild the complete Studio v2 search index and record document count, vocabulary/posting counts, generation time, raw bytes, and compressed bytes against the accepted DSI-1 baseline.
  • [x] Confirm existing title queries such as studio runtime and report block tokens retain deterministic known-item behavior.
  • [x] Confirm representative heading, prose, and code queries such as known weak spots, compatibility key, DOCS_VIEWER_BASE_URL, and docs_subscope find the intended document.
  • [x] Confirm a full doc_id and date-derived queries such as 2026, 08, and 13 do not match solely because of structural identity or update metadata.
  • [x] Confirm a multi-term query intersects terms, ranking remains title → heading → body/code, and one document appears at most once.
  • [x] Inspect representative high-frequency terms and confirm the payload remains acceptable for the local Studio route without inventing a smaller-than-baseline requirement.
  • [ ] Hand compact-result presentation review to the user for direct feedback; Codex does not run a browser check or add permanent browser coverage.

Gate: Present representative query results, payload measurements, exact generated scope, named omissions, and the user review handoff. Stop for user presentation feedback before code review.

Record: Automated acceptance completed 2026-08-13; user-owned presentation review remains pending. A timed complete Studio dry run skipped the already-identical generated index and completed in 1.86 seconds. The accepted DSI-1 metadata baseline at 579b3e8b4 contains 236 documents, 631 terms, 1,635 postings, 140,733 raw bytes, and 16,402 deterministic gzip-9 bytes. The full-text Studio payload contains the same 236 documents, 8,761 terms, 82,674 postings, 1,631,240 raw bytes, and 170,007 deterministic gzip-9 bytes. The 1.63 MB local file, 170 KB compressed representation, and sub-two-second complete generation remain acceptable for the local Studio route; no hard size threshold or smaller-than-baseline requirement was added.

Direct assertions loaded the generated Studio JSON through the sole shared browser-query module without opening a browser. studio runtime returned 81 results with the exact Studio Runtime title first at score 900; report block tokens returned 19 with the exact Report Block Tokens title first at 900. known weak spots returned 23 heading/body results, led by the heading tier at 700; compatibility key returned 16 body results at 400. DOCS_VIEWER_BASE_URL returned four documents and has code postings in Catalogue Works, Management Services, Management Operations, and this delivery. docs_subscope returned 13 documents and has code postings across the expected Docs Viewer architecture and delivery documents. The full identity d-20260715-094411-2b6e65 and the date fragments 2026, 08, and 13 each returned zero.

The same generated-payload assertions confirmed descending score order and unique document IDs for every representative query. The broad search query exercised all accepted tiers in order at 900, 800, 700, and 400. A permanent extension to the existing pure JavaScript query contract covers title → heading → body/code ranking, multi-term intersection, technical code tokens, unique document results, and structural ID/date exclusion; its direct run passed. The project JavaScript lint wrapper does not select .mjs test files, so no lint-only exception or new lint target was introduced.

Presentation-feedback correction 2026-08-13: exact 64-character hexadecimal content digests are now excluded identically by the Python index tokenizer and JavaScript query tokenizer. The correction removed 12 SHA-256 terms and 12 postings from Studio while retaining short commit references such as 579b3e8b4. The shared tokenizer fixture proves both sides of that boundary. The focused Python builder contract reported 11 passed; the direct JavaScript contract, explicit Python and JavaScript lint, regenerated-index hash exclusion, short-reference lookup, and git diff --check passed. Only the Studio search projection changed; no browser check ran and no other scope or Catalogue path changed.

The highest document-frequency terms are ordinary Studio corpus vocabulary: not 225, only 205, source 197, docs 194, local 183, viewer 181, this 181, when 181, current 177, and one 175. Their postings remain document-level sets split across the accepted fields rather than positional occurrence lists, and inspection found no structural identity or date leakage. The bounded working diff for SM-1.2 adds the focused JavaScript contract and this delivery evidence; routine watcher projections remain Studio-only and no Catalogue path appears. No browser check ran and no browser coverage changed, as agreed. Gate outcome: stop here for the user's compact-result presentation review and feedback before SM-1.3 code review.

SM-1.3 — Code Review

  • [ ] Review the bounded production, policy, test, documentation, and generated diff independently after SM-1.2 evidence.
  • [ ] Check specifically for duplicated extraction/tokenizer logic, Studio-name branching outside field policy, non-visible source leakage, rank drift, stale targeted-postings behavior, another scope's output change, and Catalogue Search ownership drift.
  • [ ] Review the test diff for duplicated cases, oversized fixtures, broad query matrices, browser choreography, broad-profile expansion, and checks without a unique regression.
  • [ ] Record every finding and its resolution or explicitly accepted omission.
  • [ ] Rerun only verification-budget rows affected by review changes, then stop for review approval.

No additional evidence category is budgeted here. A review finding may require updating the affected implementation step's table before new tests or broader checks are added.

Gate: Present actual review findings, resolutions, final bounded diff, remaining risks, and affected reruns before closeout.

Record: Pending. Add findings by severity, resolutions, affected reruns, and the gate outcome.

SM-1.4 — Closeout And Durable Transfer

  • [ ] Confirm the complete result and every completion claim against the accepted implementation, acceptance, and review records.
  • [ ] Update Docs Viewer Search with the shipped Studio extraction, field-inclusion, ranking, payload, and extension contract.
  • [ ] Update Document Identity only if the distinction between structural identity and human search needs a durable clarification.
  • [ ] Mark SM-1 complete and leave Analysis full-text adoption as the separate public extension decision.
  • [ ] Present the retain-or-retire recommendation for the search feature, concepts, and deliveries without deleting them.

No implementation retest is automatic at closeout. Run only documentation projection checks made necessary by the closeout edits.

Gate: Stop for explicit closeout approval.

Record: Pending. Add durable destinations, status changes, named omissions, closeout-only evidence, and the gate outcome.
